title: How do you design assessments that prove competence?
description: How to design competency assessments that prove competence: an evidence plan, observation benchmarks, realiztic conditions, decision rules, and validation.
shortAnswer: Assessments that prove competence are designed by defining the standard of performance, planning evidence that combines what the person does, what they produce and what they know, building instruments with observable benchmarks, setting realiztic workplace or simulated conditions, fixing decision rules that require every critical criterion to be met, and testing the design against the principles of assessment and rules of evidence before and after use.
keyTakeaways: Competence is the ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results. Assessment must therefore see application, not just recall.
Plan evidence from three sources: process (what the person does), product (what they produce) and knowledge (what they know and why).
Benchmarks must be specific enough that two assessors reach the same decision.
Competency decisions are not averages. Every critical criterion must be met.

Competence rules in many markets, from Japan's GMP Ordinance to ISO 9001, expect competence to be established and training effectiveness to be evaluated. Published assessment principles, such as the principles of assessment and rules of evidence used in vocational training, give a practical test of whether an assessment does that.

sections.heading: What does an assessment need to prove competence?

blocks.text: An assessment proves competence when it produces enough valid, authentic and current evidence that the person can perform the task to the required standard in realiztic conditions. A knowledge test alone rarely does this.

ISO 9000:2015 defines competence as the 'ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results'. The ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group lists role play, peer review, observation, reviews of training and employment records and interviews as evaluation techniques, and notes that course participation may show knowledge was gained, not that it is being applied ([ISO and IAF](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176/files/PDF%20APG%20New%20Disclaimer%2012-2023/ISO-TC%20176-TF_APG-Competence.pdf)). That is the gap a well designed [competency assessment](/glossary/competency-assessment) closes.

sections.heading: What tests should a competency assessment pass?

blocks.text: It should be valid, reliable, fair and based on sufficient, current and authentic evidence. One well documented statement of these tests is the four principles of assessment and the four rules of evidence in Standard 1.4 of the 2025 Standards for Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) regulated by the Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA), which have applied since July 1, 2025 ([ASQA](https://www.asqa.gov.au/newsroom/latest-news/2025-standards-rtos-commence)). They are written for nationally recognized vocational training but are a sound test for any workplace competency assessment.

blocks.caption: Principles of assessment and rules of evidence (Standard 1.4, 2025 Standards for RTOs)
head: Test
What the Standard says (summarized)
Design question
rows: Accommodates the student's needs, including reasonable adjustments and reassessment where necessary
Can someone with a legitimate adjustment still show the same competence?
Appropriate to the context, training product and student; recognizes skills however they were acquired
Can existing skills be recognized without retraining?
Includes practical application components so the student can demonstrate skills and knowledge in a practical setting
Does the person actually perform, not just describe?
Evidence interpreted consistently; outcomes comparable whichever assessor conducts it
Would two assessors reach the same decision?
Evidence is adequate for reasonable assurance the person has the skills and knowledge
Does the evidence relate directly to the standard?
Quality, quantity and relevance enable an informed judgment
Is there enough evidence, across enough occasions?
The evidence is the person's own genuine work
How do we know they did it?
The evidence shows current skills and knowledge
Is it recent enough to rely on?

blocks.text: Definitions are summarized from the Assessment Practice Guide published by ASQA, which reproduces the Standard's text ([ASQA](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/standards-for-RTOs/practice-guides/quality-area-1-training-and-assessment/assessment-practice-guide)).

Regulated workplaces elsewhere face the same question in different words. In Japan, Article 19 of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) GMP Ordinance requires drug manufacturers to train staff systematically according to written procedures, keep records, and periodically evaluate the effectiveness of that training ([GMP Ordinance](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/416M60000100179); see [Japan GMP personnel training requirements](/regulations/japan-gmp-personnel-training-requirements)). Certified management systems under [ISO 9001](/regulations/iso-9001-competence-requirements) must likewise show that people are competent. Neither prescribes how to judge an assessment, so the principles above serve as a practical test there too.

sections.heading: What are the steps to design a competency assessment?

blocks.text: There are seven steps. Steps one and two decide what evidence is needed; steps three to five build the instruments; six and seven assure quality.

items: **Define the standard.** Take the competency and its indicators from the [competency framework](/guides/how-to-build-a-competency-framework), or the elements, performance criteria and assessment requirements of a unit of competency. Output: the performance standard, criterion by criterion.

**Plan the evidence.** For each criterion, decide what combination of process evidence, product evidence and knowledge evidence will prove it. Product evidence is what the person produces, process evidence is how they perform the task, and knowledge evidence should relate directly to the performance criteria. Output: an evidence plan, often drafted as an [assessment blueprint](/guides/how-to-create-an-assessment-blueprint).
**Build observation instruments with benchmarks.** Write each observable behavior with a benchmark specific enough for a yes or no decision. Output: an observation checklist.

**Build product and knowledge instruments.** Write criteria for judging work products, and questions that probe the knowledge behind the performance, including 'what would you do if' questions for situations that cannot be staged. Output: product criteria and a question bank with model answers.

**Set conditions.** Specify setting, equipment, time, resources and assessor requirements. Where no rule requires a live workplace, a setting that accurately represents the real workplace is usually acceptable, provided it lets the person show the full performance. Output: assessment conditions.
**Fix decision rules.** State that every critical criterion must be met, how many observations are needed, and what happens on a not yet competent result. Output: decision and reassessment rules.
**Review and validate.** Review the tools before use, then validate practice and judgments after use. Output: a review record, and a validation schedule and record.

sections.heading: What does a competency observation checklist look like?

blocks.text: A good checklist states behaviors so specifically that the assessor only has to record what they saw. The extract below is illustrative, for a hypothetical task of isolating a machine before maintenance. It is not taken from a published unit.

blocks.caption: Illustrative observation checklist extract: isolate plant before maintenance
head: Criterion
Benchmark (what the assessor must see)
Critical
Evidence type
rows: Names every energy source listed on the machine's isolation sheet before starting
Informs the area supervisor and people in the zone before isolating
Operates each isolation point and applies a personal lock and tag to each
Attempts start and checks stored energy is released before any work begins
Record lists every point, time and name, legible and complete
Explains response to a missing lock point
States the correct escalation when an isolation point on the sheet cannot be found

blocks.text: The decision rule for this extract would be: all critical criteria met on two separate occasions; the non critical criterion may be corrected on the spot and noted. Two occasions address sufficiency, a named assessor with current industry skills addresses reliability, and a supervisor verification that the candidate performed the task unaided addresses authenticity.

sections.heading: How do you check that competency assessments stay valid?

blocks.text: Validate by having qualified people who did not design or deliver the assessment review the tools and a sample of completed judgments, on a schedule and whenever risk or content changes.

Standard 1.5 of the 2025 Standards for RTOs requires every training product on an RTO's scope to be validated at least once every five years, and more often where risks, changes or feedback arise, using a risk based sample; the outcome must not be determined solely by a person who designed or delivered the training or assessment ([ASQA](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/standards-for-RTOs/practice-guides/quality-area-1-training-and-assessment/assessment-practice-guide)). In European higher education, the Standards and Guidelines for Quality Assurance in the European Higher Education Area (ESG 2015) make a related point about independence, suggesting that where possible assessment is carried out by more than one examiner ([ESG 2015](https://www.enqa.eu/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/ESG_2015.pdf)). Workplace programs outside formal education can adopt the same discipline. For workplace re-checks of people already deemed competent, see [verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines assessment points against specific competencies, concepts and obligations in the framework, so each observation criterion and question can be traced to what it proves. See [hybrid verification programs](/programs/hybrid-verification).

faqs.q: Can an online quiz prove competence?
faqs.a: Usually not on its own. A quiz can provide knowledge evidence and can test recognition and decision making through scenarios, but most competencies involve performing a task. Combine the quiz with observation, work product review or a supervisor report to cover the performance side.

faqs.q: How many times should a task be observed?
faqs.a: Enough for sufficiency: to show the performance is consistent, not a one off. Units of competency often state how many times performance evidence must be demonstrated. In workplace programs, two or more occasions in different conditions is common for critical tasks.

faqs.q: Who can assess competence in the workplace?
faqs.a: Someone with current competence in the task and training in assessment. In formal vocational systems, assessor credentials are usually set by the regulator's standards, and individual qualifications can add industry currency requirements. In internal programs, set equivalent criteria and record them.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a competency assessment and verification of competency?
faqs.a: A competency assessment establishes that someone is competent, usually after training. Verification of competency confirms that a person who already holds a qualification or ticket can perform the task safely in a specific workplace, on specific equipment. The [completion vs competency comparison](/compare/completion-tracking-vs-competency-verification) covers related distinctions.
